title: FDA De Novo review of QuantX: radiologists' breast MRI accuracy rises modestly with AI analysis
summary: In the reader study that FDA reviewed for QuantX, 19 radiologists reading 111 breast MRI cases raised their AUC from 0.7055 to 0.7575 with the software.
account: Quantitative Insights of Chicago developed QuantX, software that analyzes a breast lesion on MRI and combines its features through an artificial intelligence algorithm into a single score. In a sequential reader study, 19 radiologists read 111 breast MRI cases first without the score and then with it. FDA reviewers report that the summary area under the ROC curve rose from 0.7055 to 0.7575, a difference of 0.0520 with a p-value of 0.0408. The reviewers write that the study marginally met its primary endpoint. A second method of estimating the AUC gave a confidence interval that crossed zero. Training materials gave readers an optimistic view of the software, and the case set was enriched. FDA granted the De Novo request on 19 July 2017 and found that the probable benefits outweigh the probable risks.
purpose: QuantX was built to help radiologists assess and characterize breast abnormalities on MRI. Better characterization is that purpose.

ratings.reason: Radiologist AUC rose from 0.7055 to 0.7575 with the score in the reader study.

ai_role.statement: Each radiologist read every case first without and then with the score, so the change is attributed to the software.

evidence.title: De Novo classification request for QuantX (DEN170022)
